# Web3 Opportunities — Solana, non-dilutive

_Bundled baseline as of 2026-08-24. A few fields I checked live today (2026-08-29) are marked. Everything starred (\*) is a time-sensitive baseline snapshot — verify before you act._

Solana is one of the better ecosystems for staying undiluted. There are four real routes, plus two things in the results that look non-dilutive and aren't.

## Grants (non-dilutive)

- **Solana Foundation Grants** — https://solana.org/grants — **[live-verified · 2026-08-29]** Rolling applications, no fixed deadline, roughly a 4-week review. Milestone-based, and open to individuals, independent teams, companies, universities, and nonprofits alike. This is the main door for what you're asking.
  - **Caveat that matters specifically to you:** the same application form also offers **convertible grants**, which "convert to investments only if a project reaches certain milestones, such as raising a priced round." That is *not* non-dilutive — it's a delayed investment. The trade is that convertible grants can fund closed-source, commercial work, whereas the standard track leans toward public goods. If zero dilution is the hard constraint, apply on the standard milestone-based track and say so explicitly.
- **Filecoin / Protocol Labs Grants** — multi-chain · idea→mvp — open grants up to $50k, milestone-based\* — rolling public devgrants\*, RFPs currently inactive\* — https://github.com/filecoin-project/devgrants — only worth it if your project genuinely touches storage or data availability.

## Bounties & hackathon prizes (non-dilutive)

- **Superteam / Superteam Earn** — Solana · SEA + global · idea/pre-seed — bounties, grants, and hackathon support\* — open\* — https://superteam.fun/ — the most direct non-dilutive cash for a Solana team. Earn is a continuous bounty board; regional Superteams run their own grant pools on top. Nothing is taken in return. A global hackathon on DAOs and network states was active as of the baseline\*.

## Education / fellowships (non-dilutive, but training and access rather than capital)
